items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: I would take them through a Brahms symphony

ctx.x: would conduct when John wasn’t there. Then Mel Lewis had been working for years with what they call the Westdeutscher Rundfunk, which is the radio orchestra in Cologne Germany. And he got me on that. So for two summers I conducted that orchestra in Cologne. Did the “Rhapsody in Blue” and there’s a funny story about that with Gunther Schuller. And the “Rhapsody in Blue” and the Paul Whiteman program with the full arrangements for the strings and all this kind of stuff. And did another concert with Milt Grayson who…

please if you want, take my class, I really don’t care. I don’t have time for it right now. So I called up and I started designing my own classes there, which would cover kind of like Ellington and Brahms, and I would take them through a Brahms symphony for a month or two, and then an Ellington extended work, and look for the intersections in terms of the narrative structure of composition and orchestration. I was teaching myself this stuff and getting paid for it. In the very first class at the New School for…
